steps.text: In a bowl, toss 1 cup of sugar with remaining ingredients and mix well.
Pour mixture on to a cookie sheet, spread evenly, and bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven and sprinkle remaining 1 cup of sugar over the top and mix. Allow walnuts to cool before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Brandied Candied Walnuts
raw_recipe.description: These sweet candied walnuts with a hint of orange zest are wonderful as a snack or appetizer. Try them as a sophisticated addition to desserts and salads.
raw_recipe.name: Brandied Candied Walnuts

review.reviewBody: Awesome and super easy! I can't wait to give these away for Christmas. I've made one batch, and I intend to make 2-3 more. A few tips, definitely cover your baking sheet with foil before making these. I even sprayed a little cooking spray on the foil -- not sure if it helped or not. And as other reviewers have said, stir the nuts halfway through the baking time. Also, I found I didn't need nearly a full cup of sugar to coat the nuts at the end. I just sprinked some on, stirred and kept adding a little sugar until I felt the nuts were coated enough. It seems a little scary when the nuts first come out of the oven because there is a lot of gooey syrup, but just keep stirring and adding a little sugat at a tim, and the nuts will seperate well and not be sticky.

Parchment Paper is your friend! Use it or foil to make clean up easy. I like making a small batch and then adjusting to taste. For the big batch, I didn't use the extra sugar in step 4, used the juice of half a lemon instead of OJ, added extra cinnamon and used almost 2 pounds of walnuts. For a different texture (we didn't like the glaze), drop the temp to 250 and stir the nuts every 20 minutes until you get the texture you like.

5 STARS WONDERFUL. I made them with 1 cup of sugar and baked them 30 minutes for a bit more crispness. I also chose not to cover them with the other cup of sugar and without that, they were just the right amount of "sweet" --AND not so many calories. Great recipe.

I liked this recipe "as-is". I made variations that I also enjoyed... Made more liquid than the recipe called for; strained the liquid before baking and then dipped the cooked nuts back in the remaining liquid before final coating. I used Cointreau instead of brandy. Will try combinations using brandy and Cointreau next batch. When double-dipping, I baked a few minutes more

I made these for Thanksgiving, although my 9-year-old niece did most of the work. she recommended the 4-star rating because the taste is good, but the dipping was time-consuming, and I concur. be sure to use a rimmed baking sheet. We didn't and the coating ran over the sheet and into the oven. Otherwise, great recipe that i would make again. (p.s. we did not sprinkle the sugar on at the end b/c of of our preference, and they were plenty sweet.) (p.p.s. we used cashews instead of walnuts.)

This is now a staple of my Christmas Treats. Family really can't get enough.

I add 1/2 teaspoon orange zest along with fresh squeezed oj.

Do not use all the sugar at the end. Just sprinkle a little in at a time while stirring. They will separate!

Made the candied walnuts tonight, very easy and extremely tasty. I made some adjustments.... added 2 tablespoons of molasses and a 1/4 tsp of nutmeg, and it turned out to be a good choice. Next time I will use brown sugar, 2/3 cup brandy, dust with 1/4 cup white sugar after baking. Reminds me of the candied walnuts my mother would make.
Best candied nut recipe for me so far. Used Cointreau instead of brandy. Had to make it twice because the first batch was gone by the next morning. They are a wonderful addition to apple crisp! LOVE!
I sprinkled about 1/2 c. sugar and found it more than enough. May add some cayenne next time around.
Very good recipe. loved it! I stired half way during cooking to coat well.

This recipe sounded so good and it was such a disappointment. I did follow the instructions, but the tray is ruined because the caramelization of the sugar, after being baked for 20 minutes at 3:50°, it’s so big down to the pan it’s a total mess and half the nuts are burnt.
Very faint orange flavor and gritty sugar crunch-nice experiment, but will not make again.
Made it twice because I didn't make enough the first time.
Super wonderful recipe - super easy - my new go-to recipe - great hit at our party !

I made these for Christmas this year. The recipe was simple and easy. They turned out wonderful! I plan to make them again next Christmas, but will add a bit more Brandy and reduce the amount of sugar to toss with after baking. Wisconsinites love their Brandy!!

I liked this recipe as it emulates 18th Century ways of preserving foods for the winter. if these walnuts (or pecans) had not been "cooked" and coated they would have been "buggy" by winter. I am using this recipe as part of a 18th Century learning tool. They most likely didn't have oranges or juice but another "acidic" juice could be used.
Made as directed. The end where you are adding the remaining sugar, too much sugar for my taste.
Really good, really easy to make. Hard to not eat them all at once!
A truly interesting and delightful way to prepare walnuts. I love the unique flavor produced by blending of the various flavors.
